examples.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of arctangent is

$$
\frac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(\arctan x) = \dfrac{1}{1+x^2}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-7x)) \\  & =\frac{1}{1+(-7x)^{2}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-7x) \\  & =\frac{1}{1+49{x}^{2}}\cdot (-7) \\  & =-\frac{7}{1+49{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

The formula for the derivative of arccosine is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5-2\operatorname{arccos}⁡x) \\  & =0-2\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arccos}⁡x) \\  & =-2(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}) \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$
